study_design_identified: Systematic review (PRISMA-guided qualitative/thematic systematic review with descriptive study-count synthesis, no meta-analysis)
why_tool_chosen: The paper explicitly self-identifies and executes a secondary systematic review following PRISMA guidelines across five bibliographic databases (Web of Science, Environmental Complete, Scopus, Global Health, and PubMed) with title/abstract and full-text screening documented in a PRISMA flow diagram (Figure 1). Per RISK_OF_BIAS.md §1, AMSTAR 2 is the mandatory instrument for systematic reviews with an explicit systematic search and screening method.

domain_ratings.domain_name: Q1. Research questions and inclusion criteria include components of PICO
domain_ratings.justification: Sections 1 and 2 define the target populations/regions (onsite sanitation users and faecal sludge emptiers in Sub-Saharan Africa, South Asia, and Southeast Asia), exposures/interventions (manual, mechanical, and gravitational emptying technologies and improvement initiatives such as PPPs and NGO/IDA support), timeframe (January 2002 to December 2021), and outcomes (factors determining method choice, emptier challenges, and barriers), while referring to Supplementary Table S1 for detailed inclusion/exclusion criteria. Comparator specification is optional in AMSTAR 2 where not applicable to a descriptive review question.
domain_ratings.where_found: Section 1 Introduction (PDF p. 2); Section 2 Methodology (PDF p. 2)

domain_ratings.domain_name: Q2. Protocol established prior to conduct of review and deviations justified [CRITICAL]
domain_ratings.justification: The review contains no statement that review methods were established in a written or registered protocol (e.g., PROSPERO or OSF) prior to conducting the search and synthesis, and no discussion of protocol deviations.

domain_ratings.domain_name: Q3. Explanation of selection of study designs for inclusion in the review
domain_ratings.justification: Authors state they searched for peer-reviewed literature without explaining or justifying eligible study designs. Section 3.2 post hoc notes the 37 included papers comprised 17 observational studies, 10 practitioner papers, and 10 case studies (with zero experimental studies), and the bibliography cites unpublished theses, conference papers, and donor draft reports despite the Abstract claiming 37 peer-reviewed journals were reviewed.
domain_ratings.where_found: Abstract (PDF p. 1); Section 2 Methodology (PDF p. 2); Section 3.2 (PDF p. 4); References (PDF pp. 12-14)

domain_ratings.justification: Although five databases (Web of Science, Environmental Complete, Scopus, Global Health, and PubMed) were searched and search terms were placed in Supplementary Table S2, the review fails AMSTAR 2 Partial Yes and Yes criteria because it restricted inclusion to English-language publications without any justification (a salient omission for Francophone/Lusophone Africa and South/Southeast Asia) and did not report searching reference lists, study registries, grey-literature databases, or consulting content experts.

domain_ratings.domain_name: Q5. Study selection performed in duplicate
domain_ratings.justification: Title/abstract and full-text screening are described solely in the passive voice with no mention of independent duplicate screening by two reviewers, kappa/agreement statistics, or procedures for resolving disagreements.
domain_ratings.where_found: Section 2 Methodology (PDF p. 2); Author contributions (PDF p. 12)

domain_ratings.domain_name: Q6. Data extraction performed in duplicate
domain_ratings.justification: Data extraction is described in a single passive-voice sentence listing extracted variables, with no report of independent duplicate extraction or verification by a second reviewer.
domain_ratings.where_found: Section 2 Methodology (PDF p. 2); Author contributions (PDF p. 12)

domain_ratings.domain_name: Q7. List of excluded studies provided and exclusions justified [CRITICAL]
domain_ratings.justification: 94 full-text articles were excluded after eligibility assessment, but no list/bibliography of excluded full-text articles is provided (nor referenced in the Supplementary Material), and Figure 1 does not even report aggregate reasons for the 94 full-text exclusions.
domain_ratings.where_found: Section 2 Methodology (PDF p. 2); Section 3.1 (PDF p. 2); Figure 1 (PDF p. 3)

domain_ratings.domain_name: Q8. Included studies described in adequate detail
domain_ratings.justification: No study-level characteristics table of the 37 included studies (detailing individual citations, designs, sample sizes, populations, settings, technologies, and outcomes) is presented in the main text; only aggregate counts/charts (Figures 2-5) and selective narrative examples are provided.

domain_ratings.domain_name: Q9. Satisfactory technique for assessing risk of bias (RoB) in individual included studies [CRITICAL]
domain_ratings.justification: No risk-of-bias or critical appraisal instrument or assessment of any kind was reported or applied to the 37 included studies.

domain_ratings.domain_name: Q10. Sources of funding for studies included in the review reported
domain_ratings.justification: The review does not extract, tabulate, or discuss funding sources of the 37 included primary studies.

domain_ratings.domain_name: Q11. Appropriate methods for statistical combination of results in meta-analysis [CRITICAL]
domain_ratings.justification: No meta-analysis or statistical pooling of effect estimates was performed; synthesis consisted solely of descriptive frequency counts and narrative thematic grouping.
domain_ratings.where_found: Section 2 Methodology (PDF p. 2); Section 3 Results and discussion (PDF pp. 2-10)

domain_ratings.domain_name: Q12. Assessment of potential impact of RoB in individual studies on meta-analysis results
domain_ratings.justification: No meta-analysis was performed (and no risk-of-bias assessment was conducted).
domain_ratings.where_found: Section 2 Methodology (PDF p. 2); Section 3 Results and discussion (PDF pp. 2-10)

domain_ratings.domain_name: Q13. Accounted for RoB in individual studies when interpreting/discussing results [CRITICAL]
domain_ratings.justification: Because study quality and risk of bias were never assessed, the authors treated observational studies, practitioner briefs, theses, and donor reports identically in thematic vote-counting and policy recommendations without accounting for methodological limitations of primary sources.

domain_ratings.domain_name: Q14. Satisfactory explanation for and discussion of heterogeneity observed in results
domain_ratings.justification: Although the authors noted isolated contextual exceptions (e.g., higher formal manual emptying fees than vacutug fees in Kisumu, Kenya, and inaccessible areas of Bangladesh on p. 6, and higher sanitation construction costs in SSA than Asia on p. 7), they did not systematically examine heterogeneity across study designs (observational vs. practitioner vs. case studies) or measurement definitions, and exhibited minor internal count discrepancies (health challenges reported as n = 12 in the Abstract vs. n = 14 in Section 3.4.2).
domain_ratings.where_found: Abstract (PDF p. 1); Section 3.3.2 (PDF p. 6); Section 3.4 & 3.4.2 (PDF p. 7)

domain_ratings.domain_name: Q15. Adequate investigation of publication bias in quantitative synthesis [CRITICAL]
domain_ratings.justification: No quantitative synthesis or meta-analysis was conducted.
domain_ratings.where_found: Section 2 Methodology (PDF p. 2); Section 3 Results and discussion (PDF pp. 2-10)

domain_ratings.domain_name: Q16. Potential sources of conflict of interest and review funding reported
domain_ratings.justification: The Conflict of interest section explicitly declares that the research was conducted in the absence of any commercial or financial relationships that could be construed as a potential conflict of interest (meeting AMSTAR 2 criteria, though no separate funding grant statement is listed).

cross_tool_domains.attrition: Cannot tell / High concern at review selection stage: Primary-study attrition was never appraised by the review authors; at the review level, 94 of 131 full-text articles were excluded without reporting any exclusion reasons or whether full texts were unretrievable (Figure 1, p. 3).
cross_tool_domains.confounding: High concern: The review performed no risk-of-bias appraisal of confounding in the 37 included observational, practitioner, and case-study papers and did not stratify thematic vote-counting by study design or methodological rigor (pp. 2, 4).
cross_tool_domains.legal_measurement_quality: Weak / High concern: Institutional and regulatory challenges (such as the illegality of manual emptying in India, Kenya, Ghana, and Bangladesh, licensing, municipal taxes, and PPP arrangements) were summarized strictly from secondary statements in included articles without citing primary statutes, municipal bylaws, or standardized legal coding criteria (Section 3.4.1, p. 7; Section 3.4.5, pp. 8-9; Section 3.5.1, p. 9).
cross_tool_domains.measurement_bias: High concern: Data extraction was not reported as conducted in duplicate, no coding definitions or inter-rater reliability checks were described, no individual study table was presented, and thematic vote-counting exhibited internal numerical inconsistency (health challenges reported as n = 12 in the Abstract, p. 1, vs. n = 14 in Section 3.4.2, p. 7).
cross_tool_domains.outcome_measurement_quality: Weak / High concern: Emptying technology choices, service quality, financial viability, occupational health hazards, and PPP outcomes were synthesized via raw publication frequency counts without standardized quantitative definitions or evaluation of measurement validity in the underlying primary studies (Sections 3.3-3.5, pp. 4-10).
cross_tool_domains.reporting_bias: High concern: No pre-registered protocol or prior analysis plan (e.g., PROSPERO) was reported, publication bias was not assessed, neither a master table of the 37 included studies nor a list/reasons for the 94 excluded full texts was provided in the main text, and minor count discrepancies appear between the Abstract and main text (pp. 1-4).
cross_tool_domains.selection_bias: High concern: Although five bibliographic databases were searched for 2002-2021, the review restricted to English-language peer-reviewed literature without justification (omitting Francophone and Lusophone Sub-Saharan African and local Asian literature), did not report duplicate independent screening, gave no exclusion reasons for 94 excluded full texts, and inconsistently cited theses, conference proceedings, and donor reports despite claiming a peer-reviewed journal restriction (pp. 1-4, 12-14).

overall_narrative_summary: Muoghalu, Semiyaga, and Manga (2023) conducted a PRISMA-guided systematic review of 37 publications (2002-2021) examining faecal sludge emptying technology choices, operator challenges, and improvement initiatives across Sub-Saharan Africa, South Asia, and Southeast Asia. Appraised under AMSTAR 2, overall confidence in the review's results is Critically Low due to five critical flaws (Q2, Q4, Q7, Q9, and Q13) alongside multiple non-critical weaknesses (Q3, Q5, Q6, Q8, Q10, and Q14). Specifically, the authors reported no pre-registered or a priori protocol (Q2); did not justify restricting searches to English-language literature despite covering Francophone/Lusophone Africa and Asia, nor describe systematic grey-literature or reference-list searching (Q4); provided neither a bibliography nor aggregate exclusion reasons for the 94 excluded full-text articles (Q7); conducted no risk-of-bias or quality appraisal of the 37 included studies (Q9); and consequently did not account for primary-study risk of bias when synthesizing results via unadjusted publication vote-counting (Q13). In addition, duplicate independent screening and data extraction were not reported (Q5, Q6), no master table of the 37 included studies was presented in the main text (Q8), grey literature/theses/reports were cited despite a stated peer-reviewed journal restriction (Q3), and minor numerical inconsistencies occurred between the Abstract (health challenges n = 12) and Section 3.4.2 (n = 14).
